prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D layout as the camera wearer turns clockwise from a dark counter in Frame 1 to walk past a dining table (moving from ~2.5 m away on the right in Frame 2 to ~0.5–1.2 m on the left in Frames 4–5) surrounded by chairs (~0.8–2 m away) and a close right-hand cabinet or partition (~0.4–0.8 m away in Frames 2–4). In Frame 1, bright foreground values clearly separate the camera wearer's extended left and right arms (~0.3–0.5 m, within arm's reach of kitchenware below) and a round pan (~0.7 m on the right) from the dark background recess, which is nearly invisible in the dimly lit RGB frame alone. In Frames 4 and 5, the map resolves a second person standing ~2–3 m ahead-right (~1 m behind the table and back chair) who faces toward the camera wearer while holding a tablet within their left arm's reach (~0.3 m from their body), with their head and upper chest cropped above the top frame edge and the foreground chair partially occluding the table corner. However, the depth map is unreliable in maintaining consistent absolute scale across frames (normalizing the floor and wall brighter in Frame 2 than in Frames 4–5), flattens small bowls and jars into the tabletop surface, and loses background geometry in the pitch-black upper regions of Frames 4 and 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map is sparse across the sequence, detecting nothing in the dark counter scene of Frame 1 or the room transition of Frame 2, and omitting the dining table, floor, walls, and the camera wearer's hands throughout. In Frame 3, as the camera wearer approaches to ~1.5 m from the table, it isolates a small "bowl" on the left edge (~1.5 m away) and a "bottle" ~0.5 m further back and higher up on the tabletop (~2 m away), which helps separate individual containers from the cluttered surface in the RGB image. In Frame 4, it segments the lower torso and legs of the standing person at the top-right (~3 m away, facing toward the camera wearer with their upper body cropped out and standing ~1.5 m behind the table), alongside a small bowl within the camera wearer's arm's reach on the near-left table edge (~0.8 m) and the close partition on the bottom-right (~0.6–1 m, partly out of view). The map is highly unreliable in both recall and classification, missing most chairs and tableware while mislabelling the near tabletop bowl as "mouse" and the right partition as "umbrella" in Frame 4, and misclassifying the standing person's dark trousers (~2–2.5 m ahead-right) as a "chair" in Frame 5.
descriptions.pose: In Frame 1, the pose map renders a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's extended right hand (~0.4 m ahead-left, within arm's reach of the vessels below), clearly showing the wrist and finger articulation reaching toward a container despite heavy motion blur and darkness in the RGB image. However, it misses the camera wearer's left hand and forearm (~0.3 m away on the far left, partially occluded by the frame boundary) and outputs no body or hand skeletons at all in Frames 2 through 5. Consequently, the pose map alone cannot show the camera wearer's rightward turn and approach toward the dining table (from ~2.5 m to ~0.5 m across Frames 2–5) or the spatial layout of the furniture and kitchenware. It is particularly unreliable in Frames 4 and 5, where it completely fails to detect the torso, arms, and hands of the person standing ~2–3 m ahead-right facing the camera wearer (whose head is cropped out at the top edge and who holds a tablet within reach of their left hand).
